walkthroughs.body_html:
Data Types & Structures — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Data Types & Structures brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Data Types & Structures.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which term is defined as: “Base-2 representation using only 0s and 1s.”?
Which term is defined as: “Base-16, a shorthand for binary (0–9, A–F).”?
Which term is defined as: “A bit is one binary digit; 8 bits make a byte.”?
Which term is defined as: “ASCII and Unicode represent text as binary codes.”?
Which term is defined as: “Images stored as pixels with a colour depth.”?
Which term is defined as: “Sound sampled at a rate and bit depth to store digitally.”?
